body:
## Problem and result

The current V39 policy path had adjacent checks for hard invalidation, verified cancellation, and fresh-source recovery, but no single replay placed a health recovery inside the invalidated cover's terminal wait while the original planner answer was still pending. This evidence package freezes that sequence against current main and shows that the recovered full observation becomes the next fresh source, while the old answer remains rejected even when a fake planner labels it eligible.

Health 100 → 80 crosses the authored floor 88. Health 96 arrives during the matching cancel wait. The cancellation terminal carries a verified-empty fixture receipt; after the recovered full frame reaches the answer-boundary drain, current-source admission uses sequence 12 / health 96 / ammo 4. Executor cancellation precedes planner interruption, and production final admission remains `REJECTED_POLICY_INVALIDATED` with no Executor admission or input authority.

## Validation

- Candidate passes normally and under `python -O`.
- The existing pending-observation drain and dual-signal suites pass 40/40.
- Independent source/result audit passes eight assertions and rejects three altered-result mutations.
- All raw outputs, exits, hashes, and the transparent initial harness attempts are retained in `research/doom/v39_hard_recovery_pending_a01_20261009/`.

No production code changed. This is a deterministic local construction only. It does not establish live screen recognition/cadence, physical per-key release, independently useful feedback, bounded live recovery, ammo/progress effect, or a Doom/MAP01 outcome. The private game lane is still unassigned, so Issue #59 remains open.

comments.body: Scope correction from the current PR head (`e27c0b43625bbe986b8363c448e52abdb20ebc10`): `research/doom/v39_hard_recovery_pending_a01_20261009/run_experiment.py` consumes the recovery observation and matching terminal in `wait`, then drains the fresh full observation, and only afterward starts the planner future and interrupts it. So this candidate does not place a pending planner answer across the cancellation terminal wait, despite the PR description. It supports the narrower local claim that a later eligible result is rejected after a prior hard invalidation; it does not test the stated temporal overlap. No live/WSLc conclusion follows.

Review finding (scoped replay; not an approval): the test does not currently exercise the pending-planner-during-cancel-wait conjunction stated in the H/PR description. In `run_experiment.py:30-37`, it drains the typed recovery and matching terminal, then drains the recovered full frame and builds a fresh monitor; only afterward, at lines 38-46, it creates and interrupts the fake planner. The recorded executor-cancel → planner-interrupt order therefore happens after terminal closure, unlike production `cancel_invalidated_cover`, which cancels and interrupts before waiting for the terminal. Please either revise the harness so the planner is already pending while the cancel is sent and recovery arrives during that wait, or narrow the claim to separate recovery-drain and final-admission properties. The health guard/source checks remain useful; this finding is limited to whether the advertised interleaving was exercised.

title: research(#59): test health recovery during cover cancellation
